report.answer_text:
The most recent example is Justice Dalveer Bhandari of India.
He became a judge of the Supreme Court of India on 28 October 2005.[1]
He served there for about seven years and resigned in 2012.[2]
He was then appointed a judge of the International Court of Justice.[2]
In 2017 he was re-elected to a nine-year term beginning on 6 February 2018.[3]
He sat on the ICJ bench that decided the Kulbhushan Jadhav case.[2]
Other Indian jurists have also served on the ICJ. Four Indians have served on the ICJ: Sir Benegal Rau (1952–1953), Justice Nagendra Singh (1973–1988, President 1985–1988), Justice R.S. Pathak (1989–1991) and Justice Dalveer Bhandari (2012–present).[4] Nagendra Singh was not a Supreme Court judge. Pathak was, and he was also Chief Justice of India.
Bhandari's current term runs out in early 2027. I didn't find confirmed results for the November 2026 election, so check the ICJ or UN websites for the latest.
If you meant a judge from another country, tell me which one and I'll look into it.
